title: Curve get_virtual_price in checkBalance enables flash-loan yield inflation
one_line_summary: checkBalance uses get_virtual_price() which can be temporarily inflated, causing the strategy to report a balance larger than real assets held
setup_steps: Define a function `check_balance(lp_tokens: u128, virtual_price: u128, weth_balance: u128) -> u128` that exactly mirrors the Solidity logic: `weth_balance + (lp_tokens * virtual_price) / WAD`
Establish a baseline scenario: lp_tokens = 1000 * WAD (1000 LP tokens), normal_virtual_price = 1_010_000_000_000_000_000u128 (1.01 * 1e18, typical Curve VP), weth_balance = 0
Establish an inflated scenario: same lp_tokens, inflated_virtual_price = 1_060_000_000_000_000_000u128 (1.06 * 1e18, ~5% inflation from large single-sided deposit), weth_balance = 0
preconditions: LP token balance is non-zero (strategy holds LP tokens in gauge)
get_virtual_price() returns a value that has been temporarily inflated by a large single-sided add_liquidity in the same block
No additional checks constrain the reported balance beyond this simple multiplication
execution_steps: Step 1: Call check_balance with normal_virtual_price to get baseline_balance
Step 2: Call check_balance with inflated_virtual_price to get inflated_balance
Step 4: Assert inflated_balance > baseline_balance (bug: the function reports more value than is actually backed)
Step 5: Assert phantom_yield == lp_tokens * (inflated_virtual_price - normal_virtual_price) / WAD (i.e., exactly 50 WETH worth of phantom yield for 1000 LP tokens at 5% VP inflation)
Step 6: Assert that phantom_yield > 0 and equals 50 * WAD (50 ether units of phantom balance)

assertions.explanation: With normal VP of 1.01, 1000 LP tokens correctly map to 1010 WAD worth of assets

assertions.expected_value: Should equal baseline_balance (1010 WAD) because no real assets changed
assertions.explanation: After flash-loan single-sided deposit inflates VP by 5%, checkBalance reports 50 WAD more than real backing - this phantom yield is what gets distributed as OETH rebases

assertions.expected_value: 0 (no real assets were added to the strategy)
assertions.explanation: The difference between inflated and baseline balance is entirely unbacked phantom value caused by temporary VP inflation; if rebase() is called at this moment, OETH is minted against this phantom yield

failure_modes: The pure arithmetic test does not prove the full exploit chain (flash loan + rebase trigger) - it only proves the accounting vulnerability in the checkBalance formula
The actual VP inflation achievable may differ from 5% depending on pool depth and composition - the test uses an illustrative figure
The test cannot prove the rate limiter bypass without a full fork test - it only shows the raw accounting exposure
If the repository is Rust/Soroban but the bug is in a Solidity contract, there may be no Cargo.toml to link against - this test is pure arithmetic requiring no external dependencies
The Cargo.toml for the PoC must be created from scratch as a standalone crate since the bug is in a Solidity contract not a Soroban contract
The privileged precondition (operator/strategist role required to call rebase) means the full exploit requires elevated access - the arithmetic PoC still demonstrates the core accounting flaw
